label: early-sequence memory of a z/x/n/f/c-initial sequence, read out at <DEL> and on i/u/h/m/b inputs
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase (t>=2, peaking t=3-5) and at the <DEL> step (about 49% of activation mass); it essentially never fires in the copy phase after <DEL>. It depends strongly on the first original token: z (6.9x), x, n, f, c. A second original token from a similar set (z/x/n/f/c/s/r/o/w) raises precision. Within the original phase it fires on the first occurrence of i, u, h, m or b inputs. Strongest activations are at <DEL> for short sequences that start with z then n/f/z/x (e.g. z n u <DEL>). Magnitude goes down as more tokens come after the opening pair, and it is lower when the sequence has digits. It does not fire at t<2, on repeated tokens, or after the delimiter. This looks like a graded hidden-state readout, so the boolean predicate captures only about half the activations: test F1 about 0.5, mass recall about 0.57.
